title: Best Running Shoes for Beginners in India (2026)
summary: Three first running shoes for India: Kalenji Run Active, Puma Electrify NITRO 4 and Velocity NITRO 5, based on shop pages and maker guides.
description: Helps new runners in India pick a first pair: Kalenji Run Active, Puma Electrify NITRO 4 and Velocity NITRO 5, compared from shop pages and guides.
lead: Which running shoe should a new runner buy in India? Here are three picks from three tiers. One is a simple shoe for light jogging. One is an everyday road shoe. One is a neutral daily trainer for people who plan to run often. We read the shop pages and maker guides and did not hand-test any shoe. Stock can change, so check your size before you buy.

picks.name: Kalenji Run Active (men's, Comfort Fit)
picks.label: For first-timers
picks.verdict: A simple first pair for light, occasional jogging. Decathlon says it is made for up to 10 km a week, and the page shows a 30-day exchange.
paragraphs: Kalenji is a Decathlon running brand. The page calls this a lightweight, cushioned shoe for running up to 10 km a week. It also mentions a flexible sole and heel cushioning. The limit is clear, which helps a new runner who is not sure how much they will run.

The page does not give the weight, the heel-to-toe drop (how much higher the heel sits than the toe) or the upper material. The sizes shown are in UK sizes, from 6.5 to 12, but they skip 9 and 10. The size list was still loading on the page, so check that your size is open for sale. This is the men's version. We did not look for a women's one.
good: Decathlon says it is made for up to 10 km a week, which suits light jogging as a first pair.
The page describes a cushioned, lightweight shoe with a flexible sole.
Decathlon India shows a 30-day exchange and a 2-year warranty, which gives room to fix a wrong size.
The page shows a rating of 4.6 out of 5 from about 9.6 thousand reviews. We did not read the review text.
not_good: It is meant for up to 10 km a week only, so you may outgrow it as you run more.
The page gives no weight, drop or upper material, so it is hard to compare closely with the other two.
The listed sizes skip 9 and 10, so check that your size is there first.

picks.name: Puma Electrify NITRO 4 (men's, road)
picks.label: For everyday road runs
picks.verdict: A neutral everyday road shoe that Puma's own beginner guide lists for new runners. Its page gives the drop and stack height.
paragraphs: Puma describes the fourth Electrify as a daily shoe for road runners. The Puma India page lists a regular fit, neutral support and an engineered mesh upper with breathable and stretch zones. The midsole mixes NITROFOAM, a lightweight foam, with PROFOAMLITE, an EVA foam. The outsole is PUMAGRIP rubber.

The page lists a 10 mm heel-to-toe drop and a stack height of 35 mm at the heel and 25 mm at the front. Puma's beginner guide lists this shoe for new runners and for short to medium-distance training. That is the maker's own view, not an independent one. The page gives no weight and no rating. Some colours may be sold out, so check your colour and size. This is the men's road version.
good: Puma India lists neutral support, a 10 mm drop and a 35 mm / 25 mm stack height, so the key specs are on the page.
Puma's beginner guide lists it for new runners and for short to medium-distance training.
The Puma page lists an engineered mesh upper and a PUMAGRIP rubber outsole.
Puma India shows free returns within 10 days of delivery on qualifying orders.
not_good: The page does not give the weight or say how soft the cushioning is.
No customer rating was shown on the page, so there is no buyer feedback to report.
The beginner advice comes from Puma's own guide, and the return window is shorter than Decathlon's.
Stock can depend on the colour and size you want.
picks.search_query: Puma Electrify NITRO 4 men running shoes

picks.name: Puma Velocity NITRO 5 (men's, road)
picks.label: For regular runners
picks.verdict: A neutral daily trainer with medium cushioning and an 8 mm drop on its page. It may be more shoe than you need if you are not sure you will keep running.
paragraphs: The Puma India page lists NITROFOAM cushioning, an engineered mesh upper and a PUMAGRIP outsole. The details list shows road running, neutral pronation (no extra support built in for feet that roll inward), medium cushioning and an 8 mm heel-to-toe drop. Puma lists an average life of 800 km. That is the maker's own figure. Puma also sells a Wide version.

Puma's beginner guide says the Velocity NITRO suits 5K and 10K training and first-race preparation. The details list marks the runner type as Frequent, so a person who runs only now and then may prefer a simpler shoe. The page gives no weight and no rating. Some colours may be sold out, so check your colour and size.
good: The Puma page lists neutral support, medium cushioning, an 8 mm drop and an 800 km average life, so the key specs are on the page.
Puma's beginner guide says it suits 5K and 10K training and first-race preparation.
Puma sells a Wide version of the same shoe, which may help if regular shoes feel tight across the front of the foot.
Puma India shows free returns within 10 days of delivery on qualifying orders.
not_good: The details list the runner type as Frequent, so it may suit regular runners better than very occasional ones.
The page does not give the weight, and no customer rating was shown.
The 800 km life and the beginner fit both come from Puma, not from an independent source.
Stock can depend on colour and size, and the return window is shorter than Decathlon's.

choose.heading: Fit comes first
choose.text: Nike's running guide says to leave about a thumb's width between your big toe and the end of the shoe. Puma's guide says about the same and adds that you should try shoes with the socks you will run in. Puma says a slightly bigger shoe is better than a tight one.

choose.heading: Try shoes on later in the day
choose.text: Nike's guide says feet tend to widen through the day. So a shoe that fits in the morning may feel tight in the evening. If you can, try shoes on in the afternoon or evening.

choose.heading: Pick a road shoe for road running
choose.text: Nike's guide says road shoes suit pavement, and trail shoes give extra grip on uneven ground. Puma's guide says a normal road shoe is usually enough for flat, dry paths. Check that the page says road running.

choose.heading: Neutral or stability
choose.text: A neutral shoe has no extra support built in. A stability shoe adds support. Puma's guide says comfort matters more than technical terms for first-time runners. It describes ForeverRun NITRO as its stability shoe. If you are unsure which type you need, a shoe shop can help you decide.

choose.heading: Read the maker's stated use
choose.text: Decathlon says the Run Active is for up to 10 km a week. Puma's Velocity NITRO 5 page marks the runner type as Frequent. These notes tell you when a shoe may be too simple, or more than you need.

choose.heading: Check returns, stock and the seller
choose.text: Decathlon India shows a 30-day exchange and a 2-year warranty on the Run Active. Puma India shows free returns within 10 days of delivery on qualifying orders. Stock can differ by colour and size, so check your exact size first. Buy from the maker's store or an authorised seller.

faq.q: Which of these is the easiest first pair?
faq.a: The Kalenji Run Active is made for light running of up to 10 km a week, and the Decathlon India page shows a 30-day exchange. Puma's own guide lists the Electrify NITRO for new runners. It says the Velocity NITRO suits 5K and 10K training.

faq.q: Do I need a stability shoe as a beginner?
faq.a: Puma's guide says comfort matters more than technical terms for first-time runners. This is general advice and not a fitting. A shoe shop can help you decide.

It is how much higher the heel sits than the front of the shoe. Puma's guide says beginners need not think about it much. The Puma pages list 10 mm for the Electrify NITRO 4 and 8 mm for the Velocity NITRO 5.

faq.q: How do I know when to replace my shoes?
faq.a: Nike's guide gives a general guideline of every 300 to 500 miles. That is about 480 to 800 km, by our own sum. Puma lists an average life of 800 km for the Velocity NITRO 5. Look at the sole and cushioning too, and replace the pair when they look worn.

faq.q: Should I buy online or in a store?
faq.a: A store is better for fit, because you can try the shoe on. If you buy online, check the return window and the seller name first.
